item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q024_fibronectin_fragment_selection","answer":"In SCOPe 2.08, d1uc6a1 and d1o5dt2 genuinely share the Fibronectin type III family b.1.2.1 (family SUNID 49266), which is stronger evolutionary evidence than merely sharing superfamily b.1.2 or fold b.1. d1o5dt2 nevertheless has the domain-level “fr” caveat: it is missing more than one-third of the common structure and/or sequence. Align it only over confidently corresponding observed regions; mask or terminal-gap its absent portion rather than treating the missing residues as substitutions, deletions, or evidence of structural divergence. For a general full-family alignment or representative, prefer a complete domain such as d1uc6a1, all else equal. Do not select solely by experimental quality: 1o5d is a 2.05 Å X-ray structure with higher SPACI/AEROSPACI than the 1uc6 NMR entry, so d1o5dt2 may still be the better template for its retained local region or CR9-bound context, but it cannot support modeling or comparison of the missing family core. Consequently, retain it as a flagged partial member rather than discarding it, down-weight or exclude it from length distributions, coverage-based clustering, consensus construction, and full-domain representative sets, and do not count its truncation as family diversity. Biological diversity should be inferred from comparable covered residues and complete domains. Finally, shared family membership supports homology but not unrestricted function transfer: d1uc6a1 is from ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha, whereas d1o5dt2 is from the extracellular region of human tissue factor and is annotated as complexed with CR9; those protein identities, ligand context, and specific functions must not be transferred between them without independent functional evidence.","evidence_used":["mcp__scope__compare_scop_domains","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1uc6a1/homology","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/annotations","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1o5dt2/homology","mcp__scope__compare_structure_quality","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1uc6/quality","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1o5d/quality"]}]}
